claim: A nootropic is basically anything that's really a cognitive enhancer, enhancing brain power
Technically there are a couple of qualifications for a nootropic, but any cognitive enhancer is generally called that
Four nootropics, grown to love over the years, made a meaningful difference in the brain personally, and "I'll bet" they can in yours too
All four favorite nootropics are essentially natural

Some drugs enhance the brain too, like a class called racetams, quite common in various forms, especially as you dig online into the world of nootropics, but sticking with natural solutions is highly recommended
Racetams and other synthetic nootropics were tried; they seem to suffer from what synthetic forms usually do: natural forms are simply much better for us and tend to work better with our bodies
The four favorite natural nootropics
Huperzine A is extracted from moss
Huperzine A basically boosts acetylcholine in the brain, a very key neurotransmitter that directly impacts brain capacity: learning capacity, memory, processing speed, reaction time
Instead of being a source of choline, Huperzine A stops choline's breakdown, keeping it active, so it effectively raises our levels
Personally, Huperzine A has incredible benefits taken first thing in the morning
Huperzine A is really cheap and works really well: highly recommended
Huperzine A takes very tiny doses, measured in micrograms, not milligrams: the recommended dose is anywhere between 50 and 150 micrograms a day; try that and see how you feel
Huperzine A is often in a lot of brain-boosting blends, and often way overdosed: four or five hundred micrograms stuck in one is just too much
Various dosages of Huperzine A were tried, and as with a lot of things in life, more is not necessarily better, definitely with huperzine
Really not a fan of supplement blends in general, for a lot of reasons, and Huperzine A highlights it: get it directly
Huperzine A is easy to get, all over Amazon, quality brands in local health food stores; very cheap and very effective
Alpha GPC, alpha glycerophosphocholine, is kind of the sister supplement to Huperzine A

Huperzine A improves choline levels in the brain, and actually the body, by inhibiting its breakdown; Alpha GPC is a direct source of choline, which turns into acetylcholine, kind of the downstream form, the actual neurotransmitter
The combination of Huperzine A and Alpha GPC is really powerful for brain and body
Like lots of neurotransmitters, choline isn't just used in the brain but throughout the body, with a lot of benefits for both
For Alpha GPC, a lot of studies show improved power output and physical performance in athletes
Exercise drops choline levels, and Alpha GPC prevents those exercise-induced reductions
Taking choline prior to a workout, the power output difference personally felt is amazing; you'll feel it in your brain the rest of the day, and certainly in your workout
For Alpha GPC there are quite a few good brands; a favorite is the NOW brand, available all over and taken on a regular basis, along with others
Alpha GPC is isolated from a food, from a couple of sources including soy
Not a big fan of soy, but Alpha GPC is such an isolated substance, without soy proteins, that it seems not a big deal
The preferred dosage of Alpha GPC in most of the studies is 600 milligrams
Personally, 600 milligrams of Alpha GPC usually twice a day; maybe once a day might be good for you, depending on your volume of physical activity
When your volume of physical activity is pretty high, Alpha GPC twice a day before your workouts seems really the ideal time

Alpha GPC takes a little longer to take effect as a pre-workout: take it a good hour and a half or two hours before the workout, and have your coffee or whatever, say, 15 minutes before, since those work a lot more quickly
Acetyl-L-carnitine, covered in an episode on energy, absolutely improves energy, but most definitely the brain too
Acetyl-L-carnitine is basically a mitochondrial-boosting supplement
Mitochondria, essentially the powerhouse of our cells, are in almost every cell and especially dense in brain cells, so boosting them boosts energy overall and in the brain
A plug for fasting: one of its amazing benefits is the mitochondria boost, which happens especially after we break the fast, one of its fundamental powerful effects
Carnitine is in all our cells, and you can buy just L-carnitine
Look for the acetyl-L-carnitine form, which crosses the blood-brain barrier to act on the brain's mitochondria, improving cognition, learning, memory and mood
Acting on mitochondria everywhere, acetyl-L-carnitine also reduces fatigue
Acting on mitochondria everywhere, acetyl-L-carnitine shows notable improvements in sperm quality in the studies (obviously your balls have mitochondria too)
Acting on mitochondria everywhere, acetyl-L-carnitine improves muscular endurance
Acting on mitochondria everywhere, acetyl-L-carnitine has really wide-ranging benefits
Acetyl-L-carnitine is a favorite, taken on a regular basis
Really all four favorite nootropics benefit the body in so many ways besides the brain
Ginkgo biloba works by enhancing circulation, especially to the brain, but also the rest of the body
Ginkgo biloba enhancing circulation so significantly to certain parts of the brain gives massive brain-boosting effects, specifically on memory
Personally, acetyl-L-carnitine, Alpha GPC and even huperzine definitely bring a lot of processing speed, reaction time and learning capacity
Personally, ginkgo biloba brings a significant difference in memory
The studies on ginkgo biloba are really strong around memory too
Hormone-boosting supplements need cycling
Supplements like ginkgo don't necessarily need cycling: you could pretty much take ginkgo regularly forever and be fine, at a moderate, appropriate dose

Cycling off supplements occasionally anyway, partially for the benefit and the sort of fun of feeling them fresh and new again. Back on ginkgo after a break, more really vivid memories from the past would pop into the brain: the past kind of lit up
Beyond memory, the enhanced circulation from ginkgo biloba helps lots of aspects of the brain, and the body
Ginkgo biloba enhances nitric oxide, really important for blood flow, including for erections and exercise performance, and oxygen uptake
Some studies even show ginkgo biloba significantly improved skin moisture, "I would imagine" because of circulation to the skin
Ginkgo biloba is absolutely worth taking, especially as we get a little older: a memory all of a sudden better than it has been recently is awesome
Ginkgo biloba dose: around 120 milligrams one to three times a day
Ginkgo biloba typically comes in 60 or 120 milligram capsules, the dosage a lot of the studies and brands use
Take any or all of the four favorite nootropics: they're all safe in appropriate doses, even at pretty high crazy doses, which you don't need, since more is not necessarily better
Timing of the four favorite nootropics
Ginkgo biloba is the only one of the four favorite nootropics really recommended at night: before bed is another awesome time
Ginkgo biloba can be taken pretty much whenever; personally, three times a day, usually with each of the two cups of coffee mixed with supplements, and once again before bed
Some people take Huperzine A before bed, which will definitely bring more vivid dreams and potentially lucid dreaming; personally, it kind of works a little better earlier in the day
Alpha GPC and acetyl-L-carnitine: definitely recommended earlier in the day, first thing, then maybe midday or afternoon, whenever you have that second cup of coffee

Personally, Huperzine A, Alpha GPC, acetyl-L-carnitine and ginkgo biloba are the top four brain-boosting supplements ever found, after trying lots of others, the favorites: highly recommended to give them a shot
